Hi David / Kimberly,

Thanks for the walkthrough on Friday. We're finalizing the Order Form (attached as Catalyst_SOW_v3.pdf) and need to confirm how Redwood wants to handle third-party IP claims under the MSA + order form. A couple of asks from our side:

- Can you confirm who will accept notice initially (Catalyst sends to Redwood legal + the ops playbook address?), and what the SLA is for acknowledgement?
- We're preparing an evidence bundle (sample attached as Claim_Example.zip). What format/fields do you need from our engineering team so you can accept custody and handover to your defense counsel if needed?
- We also need a simple mutual action plan with timelines for notice -> evidence -> engagement of counsel so procurement can close the deal.

We're aiming to sign this week if we can align on notice routing and the evidence checklist.

Subject: Re: Order form: indemnity notice routing & evidence handover

Julia — thanks for the materials and the clear asks. High level response and proposal below.

1) Notice routing and SLA
- Catalyst should send initial notice to legal@redwood.example.com AND ops-claims@redwood.example.com (ops-claims is monitored by our on-call incident team).
- Redwood will acknowledge receipt within 24 business hours and provide a preliminary triage estimate within 3 business days.

2) Evidence package format (what we need)
- Required: timestamped log export (JSONL), sample output that triggered the claim, user report or URL, and the dataset manifest (if available).
- Helpful: reproducible steps, model & checkpoint id, inference request IDs, and any third-party content references.
- I'm attaching our evidence intake template (redwood-indemnity-evidence-template.xlsx). Please ask your engineering ops to map their fields to column headers; that will let us accept custody faster.

3) Defense control / responsibility allocation
- Preferred flow: Redwood to defend for third-party IP claims affecting the delivered inference outputs, with Catalyst retaining right to participate and provide evidence. We propose standard notice -> handover -> counsel engagement sequence.
- If Catalyst requests to lead defense (rare), we'll require immediate access to all evidence and a written delegation confirming counsel privileges and expense waterfall.

4) Timeline / mutual action plan (MAP) — proposed
- Day 0: Catalyst sends notice + evidence bundle to the two inboxes above.
- Day 1: Redwood acknowledges.
- Day 3: Redwood triage and confirm whether we accept defense control; if yes, Redwood engages counsel within 2 business days.
- Day 7: First joint status call; evidence exchange complete.

Next steps from our side: Kimberly will circulate a short redline to the order form (minor defense control language + evidence handover appendix) and a DocuSign-ready order form. If Catalyst confirms the traceback fields they can provide, procurement can proceed to signature.

I attached the intake template and added a sample MAP below. Happy to hop on a quick call today if that helps.

Attachments: redwood-indemnity-evidence-template.xlsx

Thanks,
David Kim
Head of Contracts & Partner Legal | Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form: indemnity notice routing & evidence handover

Hi Julia — looping in the specific redlines we intend to propose. See summary below; full tracked changes in the order form will follow as a DocuSign PDF.

Summary of proposed redlines (high level)
- Defense control: Redwood proposes right to control the defense of third-party IP claims that allege infringement arising from the inference outputs. Catalyst may join and provide input; counsel selection is Redwood's but must be reasonably acceptable to Catalyst.
- Evidence handover: Appendix A (new) will list mandatory evidence fields for initial acceptance; failure to provide those fields within the stated window may permit Redwood to request a narrow extension.
- Expense waterfall: Redwood proposes a carveout for insurance-first recovery (i.e., use primary insurer proceeds before vendor-paid defense costs), and a cap consistent with the order form liability limits.
- Subrogation / recovery: Redwood will preserve subrogation rights against third parties where appropriate; both parties will cooperate on recovery efforts.

Operational asks for engineering teams
- Please confirm which log retention window Catalyst can reasonably provide (we recommend >= 90 days for production services).
- If Catalyst cannot provide the dataset manifest, please provide the reproducible inference input IDs and sample output.

I'm attaching a one-page appendix we want to include in the order form and will send the tracked PDF this afternoon.
